newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel confident on 1997 growth, deficit goals.
newsitem.headline: Waigel confident on 1997 growth, deficit goals.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday he is confident Germany can reach 2.5 percent growth in 1997 and meet the Maastricht deficit target for participation in European monetary union (EMU).

Asked by Reuters about Germany's ability to meet its forecast of 2.5 percent growth, Waigel said, "I am very confident. These are the figures that almost all economic research institutes have. I believe the fundamental data are good."

Asked about Germany's ability to meet the EMU deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), Waigel said Germany had done everything it could in terms of budget consolidation, government austerity and transformation of the social system to meet this goal.
"I believe that under these conditions our deficit will be under three percent," Waigel said.

According to government data released on Thursday, Germany's economic growth slowed to 1.4 percent in 1996 from 1.9 percent the year before. Its budget deficit was 3.9 percent of gross domestic product.
